content.thinking:
I'm planning out the file's structure, mapping which modules to import for the builder, paint, texture, math, frame, and path utilities so the implementation stays consistent with the existing codebase.

Now I'm sketching the actual diorama design: a round sand base with a central pond, palm trees built from curved trunks with frond cards, tent shapes via lathe or extrusion, boxy camel figures, low-poly rocks, cacti, and a glowing campfire, all scaled down to miniature proportions (~2.4m base, ~0.3m camels). I'm working out the lathe profile points for the sand base and thinking through how dunes (flattened, partially sunken spheres) should sit relative to the base height.

Writing pond geometry...

I'm realizing the leaflet approach would multiply part counts far too high across all the palms, so I'm simplifying frond geometry to an extruded drooping leaf outline in a tilted plane, using zigzag edge points to suggest serrations instead of individual leaflets.

Building leaf outline function...

Each palm gets 8 fronds with two extruded parts, so four palms plus coconuts adds up to roughly 64 parts, which feels manageable. For the leaf tip I just continue the direction vector from the start point to get the endpoint, and for the tents I'm thinking a whimsical striped Bedouin-style cone using a lathe shape, alternating red and cream stripes based on the angle.

Still writing tent geometry...

Finishing the pavilion canopy with stripe paint and pillows underneath, then I'm designing a camel-building helper function that transforms local body parts (capsule body, legs, etc.) into world space using yaw rotation and scale, so I can place whimsical camels around the scene with adjustable height, coat color, and kneeling poses.

Adding muzzle, eyes, ears, and tail details, then working out how to drape a striped saddle blanket between the two humps so it sits naturally on the body's curve without clipping into them.

I'll scale the diorama at roughly 1:4.5, placing three camels—one kneeling with folded legs, two standing, plus a smaller calf at 0.6 scale—keeping their bodies chubby and whimsical. I'm setting up a coordinate transform function that applies scale and yaw rotation around the Y-axis to convert local body-part coordinates into world positions, oriented to face +Z at yaw zero.

Now I'm working through how to apply geometry, color, position, rotation, and scale to each body part, making sure the sand floor height and camel foot placement align so nothing floats or clips through the ground. I'm also planning extra scene elements like cacti, rocks, and reeds near a pond to round out the diorama.

For the reeds I'll use card primitives built from the frame helper, oriented upright with a thin rectangular profile. I'm also sketching out a campfire setup with log rods, a stone ring, glowing flame cones, a cooking pot, lathe-built water jars, crates, sacks, and a lantern glow on the tent pole, plus a scattering of palm trees of varying heights to add visual variety.

Now I'm detailing the palms with curved trunks and painted annular rings, topped with coconuts and a green crown sphere, plus a dates cluster of tiny orange spheres. I'm adding pond details too: lily pads, a lotus flower, and a whimsical low-poly duck made from three spheres, while keeping the overall geometry simple with low segment counts for a playful look, and considering distant dune humps or a stone arch for the background.

For the desert backdrop, I'm placing a flat-topped rocky mesa with sandy strata stripes near one corner, plus a trail of tiny flattened cylinder "footprints" mimicking camel tracks across the sand. I'm also working out the sand texture with mottled coloring and wind-ripple stripes using a sine-based paint function.

Still tuning dune sphere sizing...

Now I'm sketching the scene layout - placing the pond center and arranging palm trees around it at varied positions, heights, and leaning angles, then planning where the tents should sit relative to the mesa backdrop.

Checking the pavilion overhang, I settle on a smaller canopy half-width of 0.3 at (-0.6,-0.4) so it clears the base radius. Then I'm placing palm trees: one leaning toward the pond at (-0.15,-0.62) with height 1.0, another at (0.35,0.55) height 0.85, and one at (-0.55,0.4) height 0.75.

Now I'm working out the small tent position, settling on (0.7,-0.3) with radius 0.3 so the eave clears the base. Then I'm laying out the camels — a standing one around (-0.45,0.78) facing one way, a kneeling one near (0.3,0.82) facing the opposite direction, and a small calf at (-0.1,0.88) scaled down to fit between them without overlapping, plus checking spacing for a fourth palm tree nearby.

I'm also placing the campfire, nudging it away from the pond and tent to around (0.3,-0.6), repositioning a palm tree that was colliding with it, and adding jars near the pavilion along with a rug underneath. Cacti go on either side of the scene, and I'm scattering rocks and camel footprints for extra detail before finalizing the pond's outline scale.

Now I'm working out the pond details—adding lilypads and a small duck with a white body and yellow beak floating near the center, then designing reed cards using a simple SVG shape of thick green blades to scatter along the pond's edge. I'm also sketching out a lathe outline for a mesa shape.

Writing part helper code...

Writing trunk sweep and frond geometry...

Finishing the leaf outline loop by mirroring points for the bottom edge, then adding alternating green frond colors and small brown coconut spheres with an orange date cluster at the crown.

For the tent, I'm building a lathe-based structure with a paint callback that stripes the roof and gives the wall a solid cream color with trim, plus a dark door box positioned on the front.

Still planning the pavilion structure...

Adding tassels and spikes along the edges, plus a rug plane beneath, pillows, and a hanging lantern with a glow sphere. I'm also sketching the rug's SVG texture and starting the camel-building function with capsule-based body segments.

Now I'm working out the leg geometry for standing versus kneeling camels, adjusting joint positions for front and rear legs to look natural, and adding hoof cylinders with darker coloring.

Shifting focus to the hump and neck geometry, I'm scaling the hump height relative to the body's base y-offset and defining a curved sweep path for the neck leading up into the head capsule, adjusting coordinates slightly when kneeling.

Still defining geometry helpers...

Designing jars with rim outlines and dark paint bands, then cacti built from swept trunk and arm polylines with striped green coloring and pink flower tops, followed by rocks using icosahedron geometry for irregular shapes.

For the camel prints, I'm placing paired footprint cylinders along an arc, alternating left and right positions, sunk slightly into the ground. Then I'm scattering dune spheres near the base rim, positioning them carefully to avoid overlapping the pond or other elements.

I need to double-check that the dune positions plus their radii stay within the base circle so they don't awkwardly hang over the edge—recalculating centers to keep everything inside the rim.

Dune4 fits at that position too, with camel B kneeling nearby. I'll skip the bunting idea and just add a small flag to one tent instead, then move on to checking frame signatures for the card helper and sketching pebbles ringing the pond.

For the pond, I'm defining a 12-point outline using angular coordinates mapped to X/Z, with a wet sand ring just outside it and water sitting slightly above ground level with mottled teal coloring — skipping the shimmer detail for now to keep things simple.

I'll add three small pale ripple rings as thin rotated toruses near the pond's surface, estimating around 300 total parts for the scene. Now I'm writing out the full code with proper array typing for positions and scale, plus the camel's yaw rotation.
